question: Should the agent activity timeline be built as a first-class core surface on top of the metadata-audit foundation, limited to subagent lifecycle supervision, or kept as an external/plugin-style observer until the core audit contract lands?
rationale: The codebase has enough adjacent signals for multiple plausible implementations, but the public surface, persistence owner, retention, redaction, and authorization semantics require maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Build on the audit foundation
options.body: Use the metadata-only audit ledger as the canonical timeline source, then add approved CLI/chat/TUI/UI read surfaces after that contract lands.

options.title: Scope to subagent supervision
options.body: Tie the timeline to the narrower subagent lifecycle and supervision work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/38626, leaving broader tool/run audit export to a separate design.

options.title: Defer the core surface
options.body: Keep current Activity/session/task views and ask for a plugin or external observer until maintainers want a core timeline UX.

recommendation.title: Build on the audit foundation
recommendation.body: Use the metadata-only audit ledger as the canonical timeline source, then add approved CLI/chat/TUI/UI read surfaces after that contract lands.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the related metadata-audit direction and has recent state/lifecycle history that would constrain the durable timeline contract.
